One file turned Claude Code from a chatbot into a self-managing dev that ships clean code on autopilot.

It’s called CLAUDE.md — and most people either skip it or fill it with generic rules. The version I’m using now forces plan mode before any multi-step task, spawns subagents to keep context clean, and tracks its own mistakes in a lessons file so the same error never happens twice. My bug-fix cycle went from back-and-forth handholding to zero intervention.

The real power is in the verification layer. Claude won’t mark anything done unless it can prove the code works — running tests, checking logs, diffing changes against expectations. Pair that with a built-in task management system where it writes a plan to todo.md before touching a single file, and you’ve got an AI that operates like a junior dev with a senior watching over every commit.

CLAUDE.md loads at the start of every session and stays in context permanently. That means your rules, standards, and workflows compound over time instead of resetting. One file. Set it once. Every session gets better.
